citation: Serrano N, Colenso-Semple LM, Lazauskus KK, et al. (2019). Extraordinary fast-twitch fiber abundance in elite weightlifters. PLOS ONE.
population: 21 elite American weightlifters (15 female, 6 male) including 6 World-caliber females (WCF), 9 National-caliber females (NCF), and 6 National-caliber males (NCM); age 23-28 years, body mass 66-169 kg, 3-8 years competition experience
intervention: Observational study; vastus lateralis biopsies analyzed for myosin heavy chain isoform distribution via single-fiber SDS-PAGE and homogenate methods
outcome_measures: Body mass correlation with MHC IIa/IIx
summary: This cross-sectional study examined vastus lateralis muscle fiber type distribution in 21 elite American weightlifters using single-fiber and homogenate SDS-PAGE. The athletes displayed the highest pure MHC IIa concentrations ever reported in healthy vastus lateralis (67±13% combined), with World-caliber females reaching 71±17%. No pure MHC IIx fibers were found. Heavy-weight athletes accounted for 91% of MHC IIa/IIx hybrid fibers, correlating with body mass. Homogenate analysis overestimated MHC I and IIx compared to single-fiber analysis. Fiber type differences between World and National caliber athletes showed large effect sizes but did not reach statistical significance.
key_findings: Combined single-fiber MHC distribution was 23±9% I, 5±3% I/IIa, 67±13% IIa, and 6±10% IIa/IIx, with no pure MHC IIx or I/IIa/IIx fibers identified.
World-caliber females had the highest MHC IIa at 71±17% (NCF 67±8%, NCM 63±16%), the highest ever reported in healthy vastus lateralis.

Heavyweight athletes (5 lifters) accounted for 91% of MHC IIa/IIx hybrid fibers, producing a significant correlation between body mass and MHC IIa/IIx frequency in WCF (r=0.919, p=0.010) and NCF (r=0.826, p=0.006).
Homogenate analysis overestimated MHC I (31±9% vs 23±9%) and MHC IIx (3±6% vs 0±0%) compared to single-fiber analysis, with SF vs HG differences significant for MHC I (p=0.005) and MHC IIx (p=0.046).

WCF had significantly higher MHC IIa by homogenate (74±6%) than NCM (61±11%, p=0.046, d=1.39), but not NCF (65±7%, p=0.145, d=1.28). No correlations existed between fiber type percentages and snatch or clean & jerk 1RM.
effect_size: d=0.50 for WCF vs NCM MHC IIa difference (single-fiber); d=1.39 for WCF vs NCM MHC IIa difference (homogenate); r=0.919 for body mass vs MHC IIa/IIx in WCF
limitations: Small sample size (n=6-9 per group) limits statistical power; cross-sectional design cannot establish causality between training and fiber type; biopsies taken 2-96 hours post-competition may reflect acute metabolic changes; one participant had prior doping suspension; only vastus lateralis sampled.
